title: The distracting role of stress: Impaired executive attention and delayed fatigue perception
abstract: Stress delays fatigue perception and reduces PFC functional segregation during intermittent exercise, without affecting sex differences in central fatigue mechanisms.
objective: To identify the influence of cognitive stress on central fatigue and associated functional changes in cognitive and motor brain areas in men and women.
methods: 30 young adults performed intermittent elbow flexion contractions with/without mental math stress task; fNIRS measured PFC/M1 connectivity; EMG, RPE, and force data collected.
context: Laboratory-based neuroergonomic study on healthy young adults; relevant to occupational safety in high-stress environments.
findings: Stress prolonged endurance despite reduced motor performance.
Stress stunted perception of effort during exercise.
Stress reduced functional segregation in the prefrontal cortex.
Stress did not contribute to sex differences in central fatigue mechanisms.
Functional integration between PFC and M1 decreased under stress.
No change in motor outcomes for women under stress.

concepts.name: central fatigue
concepts.description: Exercise-induced impairment in corticospinal pathway reducing neural drive to neuromuscular junction.

concepts.name: functional segregation
concepts.description: Measure of task-related specialization between brain areas; reduced under stress.

concepts.name: perception of effort
concepts.description: Subjective measure of exertion; stunted by stress.

concepts.name: cognitive stress
concepts.description: Physiological and psychological response to high mental workload.

concepts.name: fNIRS
concepts.description: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy used to monitor cortical activation and connectivity.

concepts.name: motor performance
concepts.description: Measured by force steadiness and variability; impaired under stress.

relationships.evidence: Stress stunted the perception of effort for exercise.
Stress reduced functional segregation of the PFC.
Stress impaired motor performance (lower force steadiness).
Stress did not contribute to the sex differences in central mechanisms of fatigue.
Functional integration between PFC and M1 decreased under stress.
Stress prolonged endurance despite poorer motor performance.

evidence_quotes.claim: Stress prolonged endurance despite poorer motor performance.
evidence_quotes.quote: Stress prolonged endurance among both men and women.
Stress also stunted the perception of effort for exercise.

evidence_quotes.claim: Stress reduced functional segregation of the PFC.
evidence_quotes.quote: Stress also stunted the perception of effort for exercise and reduced functional segregation of the PFC.

screening_suggestion.reason: Artikel secara eksplisit membahas fatigue dan efek stres kognitif, sesuai dengan topik penelitian. Tidak ada kriteria eksklusi yang diberikan, sehingga termasuk.
